spec.title: DAG workflow and node contract
spec.purpose: Define a factory node so precisely that an agent given one never has to ask what to do next, and define how records move between nodes so the owner only ever sees a done line or a decision card.

section.title: The node contract

node.title: Every factory node: schema in, schema out, 3 retries, black box, no agent prose to agent prose

section.text: A node is one role (roles/<role>.json) acting on one ticket in one labelled herdr pane. Input: exactly the artefacts its role lists under inputs (a ticket, a pr, a record). Output: exactly one record (factory/schema/record.schema.json) and the artefacts under outputs. A node reads its playbook (rendered from the role, never hand-written), runs the numbered steps, and stops. It cannot be prompted with free text; its brief is one line: the ticket id, its title, and the playbook path.

Black box: the seat inside a node is replaceable (claude, codex, system-one) because only the record crosses the boundary. A node that needs something it does not have emits blocked 423 with observations; it never asks the next seat.

section.title: Records, not prose

node.title: factory/schema/record.schema.json: id, at, ticket, seat, role, kind, code, attempt, sha, pr, evidence[], observations[], repro, note (240 chars max)

section.text: A record is written by events/bin/event.sh (which validates it) into the event log and mirrored as a PR comment when a pr exists. The orchestrator routes on kind and code only. note is for the owner's line and the monitor's screen; nothing branches on it. A failure record must carry repro (one command) and at least one observation (path, line, saw, expected), or event.sh refuses it with exit 3: kickback without evidence is prose.

section.title: The decision table

node.title: factory/config/routes.json: first matching row on kind, code, attempt and escalations decides enqueue, wake, escalate or notify_owner; validated by routes.schema.json

section.text: The orchestrator never reasons about a record. It matches it against routes.json top to bottom and performs the first row's action: enqueue (into the priority queue for the architect), wake (herdr agent prompt to the target seat with the record id), escalate (re-emit to the architect with code 423), notify_owner (the interface agent writes one line on the page). A record that matches no row is 500 to the monitor. Changing behaviour is editing the table and running make lint.
section.mermaid: flowchart TD R[record kind,code,attempt] --> M{routes.json first match} M -- enqueue --> Q[(priority queue)] --> A[architect] M -- wake --> W[target seat via herdr agent prompt] M -- escalate 423 --> A M -- notify_owner --> I[interface agent: one line on the page] M -- no match 500 --> MON[monitor]

section.title: The SDLC DAG

node.title: SDLC DAG: request to ticket to work to test to review to merge to verify to owner line; every edge is a record kind in routes.json

section.mermaid:
flowchart LR O[owner card or message] --> IA[interface agent
request.forwarded 300] IA --> OR[orchestrator
request.accepted 100] OR --> AR[architect
graph.sh find, ticket.cut 100] AR --> WK[worker
work.started 100, pr.opened 100] WK --> TS[tester
test.passed 201 / test.failed 422] TS -- 201 --> RV[reviewer
review.passed 201 / review.changes 422] TS -- 422 attempt lt 3 --> WK RV -- 201 --> MG[merger
merged 200 / merge.conflict 409] RV -- 422 attempt lt 3 --> WK MG -- 200 --> AR2[architect verify
verified 201] AR2 --> IA2[interface agent
one line: WO-id - title done] TS -- 422 attempt 3 --> AR RV -- 422 attempt 3 --> AR AR -- second 423 --> IA3[interface agent: decision card]
section.text: Parallelism: the architect cuts tickets with disjoint write paths; the queue hands up to max_seats workers tickets at once; PRs merge as they pass, never in a batch, so a PR is never a bottleneck. Every seat comes up through the same bring-up DAG (SPEC-04): control plane, guard, monitor, log tab group, then the seat.

section.title: Retries, blocked, escalation
section.text: attempt counts a seat's tries on one ticket and stops at 3. The third failure is 422 with attempt 3, which routes to the architect as 423: the ticket is split, re-scoped or re-planned, never re-prompted. A 423 that reaches the architect twice becomes an owner decision card. Nothing waits silently: every blocked state is a record, every record has a route, every route ends in a seat waking or the owner seeing one line.

node.title: Kickback: events/bin/event.sh add --kind test.failed --code 422 --attempt N --repro "cmd" --observe "path:line:saw:expected" --evidence path; the orchestrator wakes the worker with the record id

section.title: Leases and the queue

node.title: Locks are leases with a TTL and automatic release; work is a priority queue with smart dequeue; nothing blocks on a human except an owner decision card

section.text: Every exclusive thing (a treehouse slot, a tier port, a ticket, a page) is a lease: holder, acquired_at, ttl_seconds, renewed by the holder's records; the monitor releases an expired lease and records seat.stalled 500. The queue is a directory of files (queue/<priority>-<UTC>-<ticket>.json) so enqueue is a write and dequeue is a rename; priority p0..p3 from the request, age breaks ties; dequeue refuses a ticket whose depends_on is not done (work-order.sh next is the oracle). A seat waiting on a lease does not poll: the monitor wakes it on release (REQ-status-change-wakeups).

example.text: Brief to a worker: "WO-20261010-ba08 - Vendor bearings into tools/bearings with stable, uat and dev tiers. Playbook playbooks/worker.md."
Tester record: kind test.failed, code 422, attempt 2, repro "make -C tools/bearings test", observation tests/inside.sh:41 saw "FAIL - zero page errors" expected "ok".
A new failure class: add a row to routes.json, make lint, PR. No seat playbook changes.
Orchestrator reads the note field and decides the worker "probably needs more context".
example.why: Routing is the table; a note is for humans.

example.text: A worker's fourth attempt because the fix "is almost there".
example.why: attempt 3 is the architect's problem by design.

example.text: A seat waiting in a sleep loop for a slot to free.
example.why: Leases wake their waiters through the monitor.
